minor.issue: no_last_period_subjects soft rule bypassed by the swap when lunch_break_period == periods_per_day. The function compares period == periods_per_day at lines 1450-1454 of /app/backend/routes/timetable.py, but the LAST INSTRUCTIONAL period in that config is periods_per_day - 1 (since the trailing slot is the lunch break). Result: with payload {periods_per_day:6, lunch_break_period:6, no_last_period_subjects:[X], max_periods_per_day_per_teacher:4}, subject X ends up at period 5 across multiple days in Grade 5·B with no warning. Reproduced 3/3 runs. Suggested fix: derive last_instructional_period = periods_per_day - 1 if lunch_break_period == periods_per_day else periods_per_day, and use that in the two guards. Also consider emitting a warning when the guard rejects a swap so callers know capacity is short.

rca of the issue:
Edge case: _repair_same_grade_collisions in /app/backend/routes/timetable.py lines 1450-1454 reads:
    if no_last_period_subjects:
        if o_sid in no_last_period_subjects and period == periods_per_day: continue
        if subj_id in no_last_period_subjects and o_period == periods_per_day: continue
When the caller passes lunch_break_period == periods_per_day (e.g. ppd=6, lunch=6 — lunch occupies the final slot), the last INSTRUCTIONAL period is actually periods_per_day - 1 = 5. The greedy phase respects this correctly; the repair swap does not, so a subject in no_last_period_subjects can be swapped INTO period 5 without warning. Reproduction (3/3): suggest-batch with periods_per_day=6, lunch_break_period=6, no_last_period_subjects=[Math], max_periods_per_day_per_teacher=4 ⇒ Grade 5·B gets Math at TUE/WED/FRI P5. Mitigation: compute last_instructional_period inside the function (or pass it in from /suggest-batch which already knows lunch_break_period) and use that in both guards. Also emit a warning when a candidate swap is rejected for this reason so users see capacity pressure.
